aiDecision.thesis: A freshly created single-transaction contract forwarding its entire balance through an intermediate deposit address into Binance's hub is the signature of automated routing (custody/OTC/ops funding), not of a holder deciding to distribute. LINK-to-Binance blocks of this shape recur and are routinely absorbed by $267M of daily volume.
aiDecision.rationale: Depositor facts argue against real supply: isContract, txCount 1, 100% of balance, routed viaDepositAddress into a labelled hub, with a balanceBefore/amount mismatch implying pass-through rather than a held position. $51M is only ~19% of daily volume, and the modelled 1.8% assumes the whole block is market-sold, which single-use forwarders usually do not do. No side can be justified, so no trade.

aiDecision.thesis: An EOA with only 58 lifetime transactions sent its entire 4.5M LINK balance (~$57.6M, 0.45% of supply) to Binance's labelled hot wallet. Low activity plus full-balance drain fits a long-held holder/treasury distributing, not a market maker cycling inventory. Square-root impact models ~1.9% versus a market that has moved ~0.01%, so the supply is unpriced.
aiDecision.rationale: Depositor is a wallet, not a contract, with a tiny transaction count and no deposit-address routing — inconsistent with MM or exchange internal flow. 100% of balance sent is terminal behaviour typical of distribution. Loss path to price is the sell itself; size is material at 0.45% of supply against $267M daily volume. Modeled 1.93% far exceeds the 0.383% min edge and the market has not moved. Main risk is an unreported OTC settlement, hence moderate confidence.

aiDecision.thesis: 5.65M LINK (~$72M, 0.57% of supply) moved to Binance via a single-use contract with one lifetime transaction that swept 100% of its balance through a dedicated deposit address. That is one-off distribution behaviour, not market-maker inventory cycling. Size is ~27% of real daily volume and the tape has barely moved (-0.01% vs 2.16% modeled).
aiDecision.rationale: Fresh contract, txCount 1, full-balance sweep to a labelled Binance hub is the canonical supply-to-exchange fingerprint; MMs and custodians show repeated two-way flow, which is absent. Block is material against $267M daily volume and essentially unpriced. Confidence capped because large LINK programmatic transfers to exchanges have historically sometimes been operational, and balanceBefore/amount are inconsistent in the evidence.
